instruction: Run every `queued` row of JSTOR-QUEUE.tsv on www.jstor.org in the logged-in browser, a few seconds apart, at most sixty per sitting; write hits (title | author | journal | year | pages | stable URL; or 'no hits') into the hits column, status done <date>; read the articles that could print or discuss the letter and log each in the target's AUDIT.md 'JSTOR' section.

HathiTrust full-text search for the E4 and E5 telegram phrases listed in ciphers/eckert-1864/AUDIT.md (second audit section) and 'Fox to Butler' 'April 21, 1864'; record hits or 'no hits' in AUDIT.md.

In the browser (it passes Gallica's challenge) open https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k5039434/texteBrut (Camusat 1619) and https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k204021j/texteBrut (Champollion-Figeac 1847); save each as sources/gallica-text/<ark>.txt; search for Gramont, Tarbe, Villandry, vingtiesme and the AUDIT.md phrases; record in AUDIT.md 'Camusat and Champollion-Figeac read in full (local runner)'.

Log in by hand at https://de-crypt.org/decrypt-web/login; note the exact User Name the site accepts and set DECODE_USER/DECODE_PASS in the cloud environment to the working pair. In the same browser open record 8725 (RecordsView/8725), save its page and attachments under ciphers/intercepted-royalist-1646/decode/, then browse the catalogue's Non-decrypted listing one page at a time (a few seconds apart, never a bulk crawl) saving each under sources/decode/catalogue/; stop after 200 pages or on any block. Never commit cookies or the password.

instruction: Borrow archive.org item supplementaryrep0000grea (HMC Supplementary Report 1932) in the browser reader; read pp.70-74 and the 1650 entries; write into ciphers/hamilton-1650/NOTES.md whether the two 1648 Lanark letters and any 1650 letter are printed there with the cipher passages in italics; return the loan. Notes only unless the terms allow personal copies.

Ferrari 1999 (cited on Tomokiyo's Nevers page) is paywalled on academia.edu: open it in the browser or a library copy; say whether it prints or summarises Marguerite Paleologue's ciphered letters to her son; record in NOTES.md 'Class gate, Ferrari 1999 (local runner)'.

Boucher, Lettres de Henri III, tomes V-VI (1582-83): check any e-copy you can reach from a home IP (Google Books full view, a library) for letters to Maisse marked as from a decipherment; record in NOTES.md.

Open https://www.bportugal.pt/sites/default/files/ocpep-7_t1.pdf and ocpep-7_t2.pdf (D. Rodrigo de Souza Coutinho, Textos Politicos, Economicos e Financeiros 1783-1811, ed. Mansuy-Diniz Silva, Banco de Portugal 1993, 2 vols) from a home IP -- the cloud proxy gets a Cloudflare 403/connect-rejected on this host even via headless Chromium, confirmed 25 Sept 2026. Search both volumes for the antt-linhares-chave m0002 letter: decoded Portuguese phrases "para supprir o seu lugar", "e justa he segredo ate", "pela memoria do", "ministerio"; also "cifra", "chiffre", "Diccionario", "Vieyra", and any Linhares maco 86 shelfmark reference. Record page numbers of any hit or "no hits, read pp./searched X" in ciphers/antt-linhares-chave/AUDIT.md under the LX-ED re-check section.

From a home IP (archivesnationales.culture.gouv.fr and francearchives.gouv.fr finding aids do not load from the cloud), open the Archives nationales Marine sous-série B7 inventory for 1714-1716 (Pierre Paget, vice-consul at Genoa, consul at Cagliari; roughly B7 art. 21-29) and note the article numbers holding Paget's letters of 8 Apr and 28 Aug 1714, whether any is marked chiffré/déchiffré, and whether those articles are digitised (salle des inventaires virtuelle). Write article numbers and digitisation status into the result column; no copy order. (LANE OX, 25 Sept 2026)

From a home IP, fetch https://uu.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:1718372/FULLTEXT01 (Megyesi, Tudor, Lang, Lehofer, Kopal, de Leeuw, Waldispuhl, "Keys with nomenclatures in the early modern Europe", Cryptologia 2022, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2022.2113185 -- open access, but both mirrors reset/404 from this cloud environment, confirmed 25 Sept 2026) or the mirror at https://edit.elte.hu (search for the paper title if the OpenAlex bitstream link 404s). Read the tables/appendix for any Dutch/Netherlands/Oldenbarnevelt/Brederode/States-General key, 1600-1610. Record in ciphers/oldenbarnevelt-brederode-1605/NOTES.md.

Verify the working ciphertext transcription (Thomas Ernst's BNA-checked text, used in Bourdeau's catokwacopa/ads.py) against the original British Newspaper Archive scans of the Evening Standard, 8 and 20 May 1875, "W. Str 53. Catokwacopa" advertisements (BNA/newspapers.com login required, not reachable from the cloud). Record any transcription discrepancy in ciphers/catokwacopa-1875/NOTES.md; a clean match closes the "not re-verified against BNA directly" gap noted 23 Sept 2026 and again 25 Sept 2026 (LANE CX).

HathiTrust full text/page images (miun.abe1726.0008.001, Boyd, Calendar of Scottish Papers vol.8 1585-86) pp.211-212 -- HTRC EF word-count test (LANE CX, 25 Sept 2026) found "tempest","barret","cipher" and "paris" all co-occurring on pp.211-212 (control: "phelippes" hits 122 pages, confirming this is the right correspondence circle), a probable calendar entry for SP53/16 no.78 (to Mr Tempest) and no.79 (to Doctor Barret); HathiTrust's own page text/images are Cloudflare-blocked from the cloud, confirmed unreachable this session. Read pp.211-212 from a home IP and record whether Boyd calendars either letter as deciphered or still in cipher, and quote the entry into each target's NOTES.md.

From a home IP (or a real browser session that clears thefreelibrary.coms bot-check -- the cloud gets a plain HTTP 403 to curl, one attempt, 25 Sept 2026), read J. T. Thomas, "Deciphering the Code in Richard Powers's the Gold Bug Variations," Notes on Contemporary Literature 36:3 (2006), https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Deciphering+the+code+in+Richard+Powers%27s+The+Gold+Bug+Variations.-a0159331538 . OpenAlex (W337305991) indexes only the abstract, which credits the initials hypothesis to Herman & Lernout, Mosaic 31.4 (Dec 1998): 162 (see JSTOR-QUEUE.tsv row for that piece) and extends it with an unresolved family-members sub-hypothesis (Powers's parents + 4 siblings) the abstract says "proves fruitful" without stating a result. Read the full article for whether Thomas ever completes a name-by-name key for the 32 triplets; record in specs/cheap-tests/powers-1991/test1-print-check.md.

From a home browser (logged into Google Books), search-inside Ian Saberton, The Cornwallis Papers vol.6 / pt.11 (Naval & Military Press, 2010) for "16 August 1781" and "3 October 1781" and for "Clinton" + "cipher" -- the cloud-side Google Books API returns NO_PAGES for every edition/part found (PPyytQEACAAJ, WJxDtAEACAAJ, cLR9zQEACAAJ, cRl7zQEACAAJ, Q8WBzQEACAAJ), but a real logged-in browser session sometimes surfaces search-inside snippets the API does not. Record whether PRO 30/55/32/2 (item 3689, Cornwallis to Clinton, Yorktown, 16 Aug 1781) or PRO 30/55/33/7 (item 3813, 3 Oct 1781) are printed there in clear (Saberton is the editor who deciphered the "Common cipher" used by Clinton and Cornwallis in this exact window, JAR 2019 article, vol.5 p.139 for the 11 July 1781 dispatch). Record a snippet quote or page number for a hit, or "no search-inside access"/"no hit" for a miss, in ciphers/pro3055-clinton-1779/NOTES.md.
